A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same scaling-law study. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original Pythia evaluations on GSM8K, fitted scaling laws, and backtesting results in Figures 1–7 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 reports revised GSM8K evaluations and additional original MATH evaluations, including fitting, backtesting, and parameter-sensitivity results in Appendices F–G.

M1.justification: The three scaling-law forms, their covariates, and the pass-at-k estimator remain unchanged in Equations 1–6. The additional benchmark and revised evaluation sampling do not introduce a new predictive method or model.

E1.justification: v2 adds evaluation on 128 MATH competition-mathematics problems alongside the retained 128 GSM8K problems. This substantially extends the original single-benchmark coverage to harder mathematical tasks.

E2.justification: Both versions compare the compute, parameters-plus-tokens, and gold-reference-likelihood scaling laws. MATH uses the same comparison set; other model families mentioned in v2 are not evaluated.

E3.justification: Appendix B replaces v1's compute-dependent sampling target, clipped between 32,000 and 1,000,000 samples, with a minimum of 2^14 samples followed by stopping at ten successes or 2^15 samples. This substantially revises the reported evaluation protocol, although conflicting sample-count and cost disclosures prevent reconstructing the actual budgets reliably.

E4.justification: Section 7 and Appendices F–G add analyses of whether k-sensitivity and forecast-horizon parameter stability depend on benchmark difficulty. Figure 8 also newly quantifies effective-compute sensitivity to overtraining and undertraining, extending the earlier analytical penalty discussion.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the same pass-at-k estimator and present fitted and backtested curves without reporting repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The many colored trajectories represent different k values, not uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial MATH results: Figure 14 reports an irreducible error of 0.447 and compute exponent of 0.581 at k=10,000. Existing GSM8K results also change: Figure 1's corresponding exponent changes from 0.317 to 0.375, and Figure 7's gold-reference parameter trajectories change markedly. These are revised results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Section 6 adds Equation 7, defining the effective-compute multiplier as Phi(r)^(-1/alpha). The compute-optimal allocation, envelope derivation, and misallocation-penalty analysis already present in v1 Appendix D are retained in v2 Appendix E.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and discussion retain the central claims: three predictive scaling laws, k-dependent scaling, comparable predictive accuracy, unusually long-range gold-reference parameter stability, and the compute-optimal-envelope connection. The additional evidence does not substantially redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: New Section 7 interprets MATH's residual error and steeper scaling through benchmark hardness and remaining performance headroom, while acknowledging unexplained benchmark-dependent stability. Section 6 adds an effective-compute interpretation of overtraining. The limitations remove the single-benchmark restriction and explain the continued Pythia-only scope.

D1.justification: New Appendix C documents vLLM, prefix caching, batches of 128 generations, per-model A100 timings, and sampling-cost estimates. Appendix B adds approximately 500 million GSM8K and 400 million MATH samples. These substantially expand generation and resource documentation, although the reported budgets contain internal inconsistencies.

R1.justification: Section 6 and Appendix A explicitly position the theoretical derivation as a k-dependent generative generalization of Gadre et al. (2024), substantially clarifying its relationship to prior overtraining theory. Appendix A also expands the distinction from discriminative evaluation, and references are added for MATH, vLLM, the evaluation harness, and reasoning models.

P1.justification: The abstract, methodological explanations, captions, and discussion are revised; the model-family description moves earlier, and a benchmark-comparison section is inserted. The three-law narrative and most technical exposition retain their original organization, so the structural revision remains limited.

P2.justification: v2 adds an effective-compute figure, a MATH sampling heatmap, extensive MATH fitting/backtesting/parameter plots, and two timing tables. Existing plots also receive revised legends, axis ranges, and captions. The original GSM8K appendix plots and theoretical appendix remain under new numbering.

improvement.justification: MATH addresses v1's single-benchmark limitation, while clearer attribution and implementation details improve transparency. However, revised Figure 7 shows substantial low-compute instability despite retaining the five-orders stability claim. Appendix B's sample cap conflicts with its heatmaps and totals, and Appendix C uses 3.2e4 samples in prose but 32e4 in its cost calculation. These unresolved problems affect a central conclusion and reproducibility, making the net quality change uncertain.
